frequency_question: How often does a recipient state successfully establish domestic production of a sophisticated foreign cruise missile within a 4-month window of wartime mobilization?
membership_rule: Members are sovereign states at war attempting to stand up domestic manufacturing lines for complex western-designed precision cruise or tactical missiles previously only imported. Excludes basic small arms, unguided munitions, and domestic designs originating inside the country.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production of anti-ship Neptune missile (earlier phase)
Ukraine domestic production of Stugna-P anti-tank systems (pre-existing baseline)
Taiwan Hsiung Feng III production expansion
Ukraine localized repair/maintenance hubs for Western artillery (surrogates for manufacturing)

coverage_note: 4 named; small base due to rarity of transferring complex cruise missile blueprints to active combat zones
known_gaps: Extremely sparse historical precedent for transferring Western cruise missile manufacturing technology to an active warzone within a brief window.
skeleton: 4 cases evaluated from modern missile localization efforts under duress
validity_reason: Defense industrial base transfer timelines and geopolitical export controls evolve slowly over multi-year periods.
